segments.text: Welcome back to GitHub awesome. This is GitHub trending today number 61. 35 trending open-source projects on GitHub right now. Let's get into it.
Mr. Office publishes six browser editors you can build into your own app from spreadsheets and PDFs to handwriting and
code. You can self-host the editors for formats like CSV and markdown. If your app needs to edit Word, Excel, or
PowerPoint files, MR Office offers a hosted embed. Your server opens an editing session and the service sends the updated file back when users save.
Cararium runs a real Linux kernel natively inside an iOS app with no hypervisor required. Instead of emulating a full machine like UTM or
faking the kernel like ISSH, it compiles user mode Linux to ARM 64 machine code and runs guest apps through a multi-core
interpreter. It includes Vulcan support and powers the Endarium Android emulator on iPhone and iPad 2.
Mobile agent testers is a GitHub template that runs Claude code agents on iOS simulators and Android emulators
inside GitHub actions. Each agent plays a persona with its own device, font size, language, and dark mode setting,
uses your app like a brand new user, then writes a bug report with screenshots. On the demo app with 11 planted bugs, four testers found nine of them for 87 cents in model usage.
Open computer lets your team hand a coding task to an agent right in a Slack thread. tag at computer with a bug
report and it starts an isolated session with clawed code, codecs or open code.
Teammates can follow along and steer the fix before the agent opens a pull request for review. You can run open computer in your own cloud or use the hosted service.
This repo from the lean community is a verification harness for an outside lean formalization that claims to prove the remon hypothesis. It mirrors the
submitted proof bite forbite unmodified and runs it through the comparator tool against five challenge statements built
on math lib including the hypothesis itself and a generalized version for durllet l functions.
Recomp launcher helps you find and run console games that developers have recompiled to run natively on PC. Pick a
project from the catalog and the launcher downloads it from the developer GitHub release. For supported games, point it at your own disc image or game
folder to finish setup. You can keep multiple versions side by side, and the launcher backs up your saves before every update.
AirHand lets you control a remote desktop through a relay you host yourself.
Enter the other devices six-digit code to connect. The host uses its GPU to stream the screen at up to 120 frames
per second while your device draws the pointer locally so it responds as you move. If the network slows down, Airhand
skips stale frames to keep the picture current.
Son helps your local model learn from the corrections you give your coding agent. A quick pass adds preferences
you've expressed to the model's instructions. When your machine is idle, a longer pass turns corrections and tool
errors into practice examples and trains a small adapter on them. Sange tests the new version against your past
conversations and switches only if it scores better. No speaker makes a MacBook's force touch trackpad speak out
loud, even with the Mac muted. Type a phrase and the app breaks a Mac OS voice into tiny slices, picks out two
frequencies from each one, and sends those tones to the motor that makes the trackpad click. The vibrating glass produces a quiet voice you can hear. You
can also play the trackpad like an instrument.
Worker 755 is a browser game where an AI manager thinks you're the sub agent it just spawned. A task lands in your
terminal and you have 90 seconds to carry it out. The manager reads your report and checks the commands you actually ran. Meanwhile, Dan, the user
who hired it, is watching the chat with his family photos on the line. At the end of your shift, the AI writes your performance review.
Scene CV is a 3D resume template. You walk into a desk room at a rainy night window built in Blender and rendered in
the browser with 3.js. Click the computer, the printed pages, the VHS tapes, or the bookshelf to open your about resume, work and reading sections.
There are Steam style achievements, a record player, and a TV that plays your own tapes. It's all static files with no build step.
Fast Anything is a CLI and MCP server that profiles apps in Python, Node, or Ruby, and lets your coding agent port
only the slow functions to Rust. Before enabling the Rust version, it replays up to 500 recorded calls to prove the
outputs match and keeps each swap reversible. It works with clawed code or codeex and the author reports a 116x
speed up on a Python demo 2. Skill distill is a skill for clawed code or codec that asks whether an openweight
model can do the same job with the right instructions. At the end of a session, the frontier model writes a skill for a
student model, then runs the student on a clean copy of the task, compares its output to the original, and fixes the
skill at the first point it fails. It repeats until the student matches.
Wineroid is an experimental Android compatibility layer for Mac OS, Linux, and the browser inspired by Wine that
runs APKs without booting Android at all. It's written in Rust, executes dex code directly, reimplements Android
framework behavior, and draws app interfaces with Skia. Desktop builds add a cranalift JIT, and a web assembly build runs the same runtime right in your browser.
QR snip is a browser extension for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox that scans QR codes right off your screen. Press a
shortcut, drag a box around a code, or rightclick an image, and it decodes it locally with a bundled JSQR library with
no network calls. Before you open a link, it warns you about plain HTTP, lookalike domains, and URL shorteners, and it blocks JavaScript, and data links outright.
Signet helps teams track which versions of their AI agents, and skills they've approved. Each release gets its own fixed snapshot with a record of the
checks it passed, who reviewed it, and which policies applied.
Before loading a skill, you can verify the signature on that release and check whether it's still certified. If the team revokes it later, that decision stays in an appendon log.
Open Artifact lets any coding agent from clawed code to codeex or cursor create editable artifacts. You can comment on
slide decks, UI designs, design systems, whiteboards, spreadsheets, dashboards, and docs. The agent writes a plain
folder of files, and a local Damon opens them in an editor in your browser with comments flowing back to the agent session.
Void struck fits a space exploration game into a single 299 kilob HTML file.
A jump drive test strands you 2500 light years from home. You can skim a star to refuel, land on a planet you spotted
from orbit, and walk its surface. Your browser generates the worlds and synthesizes the soundtrack as you play.
Every jump home costs years back on Earth, and messages start catching up with you.
Sprite stacking is an agent skill that turns four flat pixel art views of an object, top, side, front, and back, into
a fake 3D sprite you can spin. Written in Python, it keeps a voxil only where all four views agree. then slices the
volume into thin layers that get rotated and lifted a pixel each to render. A browser viewer gives you a turntable, an
exploded view, and a 16 direction export.
Splat repair lets you brush unwanted details out of a 3D Gaussian splat scan.
Paint over a sticker on a wall, and fast fill us the surrounding wall to estimate its shape, then copies nearby splats to
patch the gap in 3D. Flat surfaces are the easy case. For a repeating pattern like the tread on a shoe, you can use the clone stamp to touch it up by hand.
Claude Multidestop lets you keep your work and personal clawed accounts open side by side on one Mac.
A bash script creates a launcher for each account, so each window has its own sign-in and chats. Both use the same
local claude code setup, so a skill you add once is available in either window.
You can also ask a running session to message one in the other account.
Antiggra dashboard is an unofficial usage widget for Google's anti-gravity app and IDE. It sits beside the model picker or in a side panel and shows
tokens per second, time to first token, cache hit rate, context window use, and how much of your 5-hour and weekly quota
is left with reset countdowns. Daily and weekly grids track your history locally.
Grid lines is an agent skill for UI alignment that draws the lines first, then moves the items. It runs a small JavaScript probe in your page that
measures the real edges of text, icons, and controls, draws vertical guides down the interface, and flags anything that
misses its line. Your agent then fixes the padding sobbars, toolbars, menus, and tables share a few clean edges.
In world's voice isolator separates speech from background noise in recordings and live audio. Give the offline model a noisy voice over and it
writes two wave files, one with the clean speech and one with the sound it removed. That lets you listen to what got filtered out or mix some room sound
back in. For live calls, a streaming model processes incoming audio with 20 milliseconds of look ahead.
Context mode for antigravity is a local first plugin for Google's antigravity app that keeps huge terminal output build logs and big files out of your
chat history. A hook blocks unbounded dumps like cat or git diff plus oversized file reads and points the agent to indexed SQLite search instead.
In the author's test, a 65 kilob unity log came back as 550 bytes, a 99% cut.
StellarHub is a control center for your Windows PC with a Python engine, and a plain HTML interface in a native window.
It puts live hardware stats, driver updates, an uninstaller that hunts down leftovers, a disc analyzer, and a
cleanup optimizer into one app. There's a catalog of over 150 apps to install, hardware and peripheral tests, and an
autopilot mode that runs your maintenance routines on a schedule.
Google DeepMind's robotics plugin lets an anti-gravity agent write a controller for a robot arm, test it in Muco, and
run the same code on the real arm. In the project's demo, a Yamro picks cookies off a moving conveyor and sorts
them into two boxes. You can also work entirely in simulation, rearrange the objects between runs, and watch a recording to see which pickups worked.
Restaurant AI skills gives restaurant teams 13 ways to use an AI assistant with the menus, bookings, and sales
files they already have. If you're choosing a dish to feature, the menu calculator shows how much each order contributes and how that adds up across
sales. When a group dinner inquiry lands, another skill helps you draft an itemized proposal with a payment
breakdown and a follow-up plan. A better antivirus isn't really an antivirus.
It's a Windows trip wire for info steelers written in Go that plants decoy files like a passwords text file, a
wallet phrase, and fake app data for apps you don't even have. When a process touches one of those baits, it freezes
that process and everything it spawned collects forensics and can kill it or cut the network. A built-in test runs a harmless fake stealer.
Work three lets you run clawed code agents in parallel, each on its own git branch with a separate working folder.
If one agent is fixing login while another builds a settings page, each gets the dependencies and environment files your team setup calls for. When a
branch is ready, one command can fast forward main to the finished commits and clean up the work tree.
Exo is a native Gmail client for Mac OS written in Rust and inspired by Superhum. It connects your Mac directly
to Google where you can read and send mail, organize your inbox, and manage settings like filters and signatures.
Setup takes an extra step. You create your own Google signin client and enable the Gmail calendar and people APIs
before connecting your account. Fast Frames is Apple's research project for generating 480p video one frame at a
time. Its two models use just two diffusion steps per frame. Give one a prompt about a surfing corgi and the
example script produces about 5 seconds of video at 16 frames per second. The repo also includes a separate Lingbot
demo where you can steer the camera as the scene unfolds.
Subtle is an agent skill for clawed code and codecs that adds animated captions to talking head videos rendered entirely
on your Mac with no uploads and no API key. It transcribes your speech with whisper down to the word, highlights
numbers and names, and picks from 35 caption styles rendered with remotion.
In the behind you styles, Apple Vision cuts out the speaker so a giant word can sit behind them.
UI diff shows reviewers what changed on screen in a pull request. It finds the affected pages and takes matching
desktop and mobile screenshots before and after the change. If a button gets wider, it can highlight the changed pixels and show exactly how much its
padding grew. Publish the comparison once and later runs can update the same pull request comment. Minecraft server
on Orange Cloud runs a Minecraft Java server in your own paid Cloudflare account. Players join through your
domain and the server saves the world to R2 about every 5 minutes. Once everyone's been offline for 10 minutes,
it saves again and goes to sleep. The next connection wakes it up and restores the world, so the first player can join again about 30 seconds later.
